## Research funding {#学术经费}

Research funding broadly comes from three sources:

- Projects funded by government bodies and foundations. In China, the State Council, provinces, and cities offer funding for projects and individuals. Overseas, government-supported academic societies also provide funding. These grants usually involve larger sums and carry greater prestige. A successful application record is particularly helpful when applying for further grants within the same system.

- Industry collaboration projects. These are generally obtained through contact between a principal investigator and a company. Most are more concerned with practical implementation. Their funding, degree of completion, and influence vary.

- Internal university research support, such as RDF. Faculty members apply for these projects; the school screens applications before a committee reviews them. There are relatively few projects, with modest funding and short durations, but they can matter a great deal early in a career.

Research funding does not go straight into the principal investigator's personal bank account. It goes into the university's research funding management account. Spending must fall within approved categories and is supervised by the university. Common expenses include purchases, conference-related costs, and payments for labour.

When a supervisor secures research funding above a certain threshold in a single award, they can receive a corresponding allocation of PhD scholarships (PGRS).

## Journals and conferences {#期刊及会议}

A journal or conference needs at least one academic organization to take responsibility for running it. Prominent, active researchers carry out work for these organizations, for example as editors or reviewers, which helps attract submissions and participation. Correspondingly, holding such roles reflects a researcher's reputation to some extent.

Publishers need financial support to publish journals and organize conferences. In general, the more important, influential, or valuable to an industry a journal or conference is, the easier it is to find sponsors, the less authors have to pay in publication fees, and the larger, richer, and higher-quality its activities can be.

The influence of journals and conferences depends substantially on how often their articles are cited. Fashionable topics, important work, well-known authors, and prominent journals are more likely to be read and cited. Organizers also give priority to these factors to keep their activities sustainable.

Many research fields have very few researchers. At conferences you can often meet people whose papers you have at least read, and even reviewers or viva examiners.

## Social benefit {#社会效益}

One way of understanding academic research is that it creates new knowledge at the limits of human understanding. From that perspective, research will ultimately benefit society.

I have also heard that researchers in the humanities and social sciences are particularly interested in work on social impact. We can invite someone to write about this when there is an opportunity.

Still, we live in a commercial society. Social benefit often comes close to meaning how much a result is worth financially, or how much potential it has. That is also the environment in which we physically find ourselves.

## Supervisors {#导师}

Supervisors differ greatly, but can roughly be divided into those oriented towards applications and those oriented towards the research frontier:

- Application-oriented supervisors generally have more implementation projects with companies or government bodies, or more application-focused government-funded projects.

- Frontier-oriented supervisors generally publish more important research contributions.

These tendencies are not mutually exclusive. But time and energy are limited, so there is usually some preference. Relatively speaking, applied opportunities are more numerous, while frontier research requires larger amounts of project funding. Supervisors develop different resources according to their interests, and the guidance we receive consequently differs too.

For these reasons, you can probably agree that there is a good chance we will come to resemble our respective supervisors.

For the humanities and social sciences, I have heard that students need their supervisors' guidance almost throughout their training. Again, we can invite someone to write about this when there is an opportunity.

## Collaboration {#subsection.teamwork}

In research, collaboration with other researchers may be unavoidable, for a variety of reasons including the following:

- Research funding. Well, they are providing the money, after all. It seems reasonable for them to offer some suggestions and be an author…

- Academic influence. Interestingly, the usual word of mouth is that papers involving a leading researcher are more likely to be accepted…

- Private data. In many fields, data not being public may simply be an unfortunate fact of life…

- Expertise. Much research spans multiple disciplines, and you may well not understand every detail. Finding someone familiar with part of the work can be very helpful: they can save you a great deal of effort and improve research efficiency. Of course, choosing the right person takes careful thought…

- Experimental work. As with specialist expertise, the right collaborator can save you a great deal of effort. And yes, you do hear of people asking undergraduates to help with experiments and then publishing together as co-authors…

Before starting a collaboration with researchers outside your supervisor's team, be sure to read the university's [Guidance on Authorship and Affiliation](https://ebridge.xjtlu.edu.cn/urd/sits.urd/run/SIW_FILE_LOAD.start_url?08F2CBCAE3174A7365Px9_5kBfG0_iGiWj8zb7ybwaO0YBYc8NiKlPG93xyQA9X2SClXOLLd7-_EgF50aijROwT-rdSGIUIbRRzhFu-76Ha0g2HymUr0S-Fgjm1DXP9RO1GhGzx5-akgsDSMBlNhR7vpib85F9vlqa67My7RKHFSiluZueFy52YCBtintt0wDTKmx4fCjkWnldNDaxo6ZVD2L572Us3V-FOv485wYZUNUn5NLzgR0pAaU7aiKnTVJY8Aa2su5F4u7o-rNPJPety3jwwJ4O1v1agpDZLZ1it1H5fWn3IgLNaWlUh84YpxNRXyTW1kIwrX0r4-dT1eoxdZUAFrJhaBwz6E0w) on e-Bridge. It may save you a lot of trouble.
